links.effect: Errors found in 90.1% of prompt 1 texts, 89.4% prompt 2, 77.9% prompt 3; only 17.3% fully adequate with prompt 3; type 1 errors (incorrect guidance) rose from 24.0% to 31.7%.
links.quote: Type I errors, which implicate adherence to incorrect guidance, occurred more frequently with specialized prompt 3 than with prompt 1 ( P =.039; Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 versus Llama 3 output adequacy and errors on same scenarios
links.effect: Adequacy comparable (P=.818); hallucinations more frequent with Llama 3 than GPT-4 (8.7% vs 1.0%, P=.008); Llama 3 had fewer task-response errors (P=.001).
links.quote: However, hallucinations or incorrect information (error type 7) was more frequent in texts generated by Llama 3 than in those generated by GPT-4 (8.7% vs 1.0%, P =.008, respectively).
